title: Over 16,000 Dressers Sold on Walmart Recalled for Deadly Tip-Over Risk
excerpt: The CPSC has recalled about 16,809 EnHomee 9-Drawer Fabric Dressers sold by a third-party seller on Walmart.com, citing violation of the STURDY Act's mandatory stability standards and potential entrapment hazards to children.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Over 16,800 EnHomee dressers sold on Walmart.com are recalled due to tip-over risks.
  • The dressers violate the STURDY Act's mandatory stability standards for children's safety.
  • Sold for about $80, the dressers were available in multiple colors and styles.
  • Consumers must stop using unanchored dressers and contact Raybee-Direct for refunds.
  • The recall highlights ongoing safety concerns with third-party sellers on e-commerce platforms.

U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission

The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission on July 23 recalled approximately 16,809 EnHomee 9-Drawer Fabric Dressers sold through Walmart.com, warning that the units are unstable if not anchored to a wall and pose tip-over and entrapment hazards that could cause serious injury or death to children.

https://x.com/USATODAY/status/2080484424102166669

The dressers, sold by third-party seller Raybee-Direct on Walmart's online marketplace between September 2023 and March 2026 for about $80, violate the mandatory federal safety standard for clothing storage units required under the STURDY Act. Only units ordered before March 30, 2026, are included in the recall, which carries the number 26-633.

"The recalled dressers are unstable if they are not anchored to the wall, posing tip-over and entrapment hazards that can result in risk of serious injuries or death to children."

— U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission

The recalled units feature nine fabric drawers supported by a metal frame and were available in white, brown, gray, and black. No injuries or incidents have been reported in connection with the recalled dressers, according to the CPSC.

The STURDY Act and a Pattern of Recalls

The recall is the latest enforcement action under the Stop Tip-overs of Unstable, Risky Dressers on Youth (STURDY) Act, which established mandatory safety standards for clothing storage units effective September 1, 2023. The law was enacted after decades of preventable deaths — since 2000, more than 470 children have died from furniture tip-over incidents in the United States, according to the CPSC.

The agency estimates furniture tip-over incidents cause an average of 22,500 emergency room-treated injuries each year, with children under 18 accounting for nearly 44% of those cases. The STURDY Act replaced a previously voluntary industry standard that consumer safety advocates had long criticized as inadequate.

This is not the first dresser recall linked to Walmart this year. In May, the retailer recalled about 165,000 Mainstays 9-Drawer Fabric Dressers — sold under Walmart's own brand — for the same type of tip-over hazard. The CPSC has also issued warnings and recalls against other brands including UHOMEPRO and EnHomee-Direct for selling non-compliant dressers on platforms like Amazon and Walmart.

Manufactured in China, Sold Through Third-Party Sellers

The recalled EnHomee dressers were manufactured in China by Xuzhou Mingquanhe Household Co., Ltd. and imported by Changsha Yiman Keji Youxian Gongsi, doing business as Raybee-Direct. The recall highlights ongoing concerns about third-party sellers on major e-commerce platforms listing products that do not meet U.S. safety standards.

Consumers who purchased the affected dressers should stop using them immediately unless they are anchored to a wall, and move unanchored units to an area children cannot access. To obtain a full refund, buyers must contact Raybee-Direct by emailing RaybeeRecall@outlook.com for instructions on identifying whether their unit is included in the recall and how to dispose of it. Consumers will need to submit a photo demonstrating disposal of the dresser to complete the refund process.

What Indian American Households Should Know

For Indian American families, many of whom rely on Walmart and its online marketplace for affordable home furnishings, the recall is a reminder to check whether any recently purchased fabric dressers are among the affected units. Parents of young children should verify that all dressers and tall furniture in their homes — regardless of brand — are securely anchored to the wall.

What's Next

The CPSC continues to enforce the STURDY Act, and the pace of dresser recalls has accelerated in 2026 as the agency targets non-compliant products, particularly those manufactured overseas and sold by third-party sellers on U.S. e-commerce platforms. Federal law now prohibits selling products subject to a CPSC-ordered recall, and consumers can report any dangerous products or injuries at SaferProducts.gov or by calling the CPSC hotline at 800-638-2772.
